{{Italic title|all=yes|string=K}}
In mathematics, '''rigidity of ''K''-theory''' encompasses results relating [[algebraic K-theory|algebraic ''K''-theory]] of different rings. 

==Suslin rigidity==
''Suslin rigidity'', named after [[Andrei Suslin]], refers to the invariance of mod-''n'' algebraic ''K''-theory under the base change between two [[algebraically closed field]]s: {{harvtxt|Suslin|1983}} showed that for an [[field extension|extension]] 
:<math>E / F</math>
of algebraically closed fields, and an [[algebraic variety]] ''X'' / ''F'', there is an isomorphism
:<math>K_*(X, \mathbf Z/n) \cong K_*(X \times_F E, \mathbf Z/n), </math>
between the mod-''n'' ''K''-theory of coherent sheaves on ''X'', respectively its base change to ''E''. A textbook account of this fact in the case ''X''&nbsp;=&nbsp;''F'', including the resulting computation of ''K''-theory of algebraically closed fields in characteristic ''p'', is in {{harvtxt|Weibel|2013}}.

This result has stimulated various other papers. For example {{harvtxt|Röndigs|Østvær|2008}} show that the base change functor for the mod-''n'' [[A1 homotopy theory|stable A<sup>1</sup>-homotopy category]]
:<math>\mathrm{SH}(F, \mathbf Z/n) \to \mathrm{SH}(E, \mathbf Z/n)</math>
is fully faithful. A similar statement for non-commutative motives has been established by {{harvtxt|Tabuada|2018}}.

==Gabber rigidity==
Another type of rigidity relates the mod-''n'' K-theory of an [[henselian ring]] ''A'' to the one of its [[residue field]] ''A''/''m''. This rigidity result is referred to as ''Gabber rigidity'', in view of the work of {{harvtxt|Gabber|1992}} who showed that there is an isomorphism
:<math>K_*(A, \mathbf Z/n) = K_*(A / m, \mathbf Z/n)</math>
provided that ''n''&ge;1 is an integer which is invertible in ''A''. 

If ''n'' is not invertible in ''A'', the result as above still holds, provided that K-theory is replaced by the fiber of the [[cyclotomic trace map]] between K-theory and [[cyclic homology|topological cyclic homology]]. This was shown by {{harvtxt|Clausen|Mathew|Morrow|2021}}.

==Applications==
{{harvtxt|Jardine|1993}} used Gabber's and Suslin's rigidity result to reprove Quillen's computation of [[K-groups of a field|K-theory of finite fields]].
